title: Between the Parked
hook: Someone steps out between the parked cars.
scene: Clear cold afternoon on a two-lane side street off the Core. Cars are nose-in along both curbs. A figure steps out from the gap between a gray sedan and a rusted van — one shoe, then a coat, then the rest. You have the paper on your side. The person is already in your paint. The plow is the only vote that counts.
decision: They are already between the parked cars and your lane. What do you do?

options.text: Hold speed — they should wait, and you have the street
options.result: You keep the number. They finish the step. The plow and a coat occupy the same paint. You dump it late. They freeze. You freeze. The side street now has a story it did not need.

options.text: Honk so they step back between the cars
options.result: The horn hits the block. They flinch forward, not back. You get a louder problem and a person still in the lane. Sound does not put them between the cars again.

options.text: Cover, slow, stop if you must. Let them finish or go back
options.result: You lift and cover. They see the plow and finish across. You never argue the paper. The side street stays a side street. You roll when the gap is a gap again.

options.text: Swing left around them and keep the number
options.result: You take the left. Oncoming is a pickup you did not budget. You put a person and a pickup in the same second. The plow cannot split that.

debrief: A person between parked cars is already in your decision. Slow or stop. Who had the paper does not move them. You saved the side street a collision.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Search gaps between parked cars; yield to a person already entering the roadway — right of way is not the question.

image_brief.camera_pose: Camera is ground level, outside the car, human eye height, standing on the wet right curb looking along the two-lane side street in the direction of travel — a rear-three-quarter, never head-on. The sloping rear engine lid of the pink Beetle is nearer the camera and large. The full-width nose plow is on the FAR front, pointing at the top of the frame. Overcast daylight, wet pavement.
image_brief.subject: a person mid-gap between a gray sedan and a rusted van — torso still in the gap, one shoe in the travel lane, not standing in the open roadway
image_brief.foreground: wet curb and a parked-car bumper closest to camera
image_brief.midground: IV-004 NON-NEGOTIABLE SET (all three, one situation): (1) pink Beetle heading away from camera, rear lid nearest the lens, full-width front plow toward the TOP of the frame; (2) that plow is the attached plate's full-width blade across the far black-tube bull bar; (3) squared in-lane and rolling with wet tire spray — still short of the person
image_brief.background: clear cold afternoon, two-lane side street, low brick, no crowd
image_brief.read: a person is stepping out from between parked cars into the travel lane
extra_negatives: no narrow flap or one-third-width plow blade
no Beetle parked or angled diagonally across the lane
no Beetle nose pointed at the curb
no headlights or plow toward the viewer
no nose-plow plate heading copied onto the street car
no person standing in the open roadway

geometry.ego_lane_side: right half of a two-lane side street
geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: the plow points toward the top of the frame, still short of the person
